newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chips lift Morocco shares slightly by close.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips lift Morocco shares slightly by close.

text.p: Casablanca stock exchange closed on Monday 0.06 percent higher with modest gains in ONA group, Wafabank and Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 637.82 points from 637.42 on Friday.
"Volumes are low on both markets, it must be the consequence of summer holidays," said a broker at Sogebourse, referring to both the official and the over-the-counter markets.
ONA, the biggest Moroccan private conglomerate, rose 10 dirhams to 785 dirhams with more than 7,900 shares exchanged, the broker said.
Wafabank was up six dirhams to 816 dirhams.
The mining firm SMI took 16 dirhams to rise to 563 dirhams with only 314 shares traded.
First tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in January 1996, jumped 28 dirhams to 1,399 dirhams.
In the energy sector, steel mill Sonasid advanced 10 dirhams to 550 dirhams with 1,932 shares exchanged, while oil refinery Samir closed unchanged at 356 dirhams.
Blue-chip Banque Commerciale du Maroc closed unchanged at 860 dirhams while Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur fell nine dirhams to 570 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private group, closed unchanged at 729 dirhams.
Morocco's portfolio company Societe Epargne Croissance said on Monday it would be delisted from the stock exchange on August 6 because its shares were not being traded enough.
Total traded volume on the official market was 24 million dirhams from 25.7 million dirhams.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 13 million dirhams from 48.4 million. ONA accounted for the main trade on this market with 6,000 shares changing hands.
